title: Prove the joint full-guard law for an overlapping corank-one pair
body:
## Summary

Scoped counting proof with finite corroboration, answering a subcase of #4240 and #4246's nonorthogonal full-guard question. For orthogonal rank-one kernels U,V on F_q^m, count one complete GL_m header passing both corank-one requests P=I-U and Q=I-V. Their images overlap when m>2.

```text
partial 2x2 Gram matrices
  -> q^2(q-1)^2 safe states
  -> exact all-field transfer law
  -> binary density:
(9^(m-1)-2*7^(m-1)+5^(m-1)) / [4(2^m-1)(2^m-2)2^(2m-4)]
```

Over F2 a common passing header exists exactly for m>=3. The passing events are strictly negatively correlated. The fractions at m=3 and m=4 are 1/84 and 1/80. No new κ or supplier admission.

Only `research/corankone-pair-header-law/` is added. Scientific base: canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19082912).

## Evidence

Before: single-request marginals do not determine the joint full-chain fraction. After: PROOF.md supplies the transfer theorem and binary closed form; three counts agree:

- 32,274 complete GL headers in seven domains, with literal no-pivot elimination for both requests and complete equal-fiber counts.
- 2,007,234 normalized pairs X,Y with YX=I_2 in 12 domains, enumerated separately from the GL census and transfer. Fields are F2,F3,F4,F5, dimensions at most six. F4 uses x^2+x+1.
- 99 transfer cases: binary m=2..64 and q=3,4,5,7 with m=2..10. All binary cases agree with the closed form. All local rank-one increment multiplicities are separately enumerated.
- Four controls distinguish independence, a lost zero factor, wrong parity and first-pivot-only admission. At q=2,m=3 the full-chain count is 2, while the first-pivot-only count is 54, out of 168 headers.

Both registered commands and both direct modes pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64. Direct normal and optimized runs took 15.16 s and 15.54 s wall time; the registered pair took 31.88 s. These are check durations, not performance claims. Each registered command has a 120 s limit. Ruff 0.14.0 E/F/B/UP passes. Four local mutations are rejected for their intended mathematical/source-check reasons: wrong binary eigenvalue, omitted zero-factor multiplicity, first-pivot-only admission and source corruption.

From the repository root, with any CPython 3.12 replacing this local interpreter path:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/corankone-pair-header-law/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/corankone-pair-header-law/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/corankone-pair-header-law
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/corankone-pair-header-law --check-source-history
```

Markers are `PASS_CORANKONE_PAIR_HEADER_LAW`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The scientific output includes every census numerator/denominator and generated SHA-256 bindings for all package files and both declared inputs. No receipt is handwritten. All eight committed package/input files and source ancestry pass preflight at `4728fc766b3084f3ab2f5c8543a5e74e4a12b126`. The official committed export and integrity check also pass. Its Git-free direct replay produces the exact same generated receipt as both committed registered modes, and all eight exported source files remain unchanged.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal claim is the written proof. The replay covers only the stated finite domains. Fixed idempotents with orthogonal rank-one kernels and a complete equally weighted header domain are essential. Only q=2 has a closed form here. Binary guards extend the algebra beyond the retained normalizer's odd-prime executable domain. No real producer, header selection/emission, dispatch, dirty return, stock, precision or complete physical invoice is supplied. Those costs remain unknown. No formal-kernel proof, selected cold replay, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Related open work

- #4227 (`3d793eade8de2ba49ec08f8d004c1b2f566a78e6`) supplies the corank-one determinant identity and marginal law. All 12 marginal fractions agree numerically here. The joint law is new.
- #4228 (`bb25dcedb5bbbacd3c35359eb6b5488b087bcde6`) supplies all-rank single-request densities. Its corank-one specialization agrees numerically in those same 12 cases; its intermediate-rank recurrence is not used.
- #4239 (`5e24dfb5463d540721687d92c369609da5589523`) counts orthogonal rank-one joint guards. At m=2 the five q=2,3,4,5,7 transfer fractions agree numerically with its (q-1)(q-2)/(q(q+1)), including 1/6 at q=3. The new case has m>2.
- #4240 (`9f9c89ed75e9fdae6b6762925b080fb308824858`) counts nonorthogonal rank-one first guards. This answers a higher-rank full-chain subcase of its first open question. Only the same m=2 orthogonal boundary overlaps, with all five numerical values agreeing.
- #4246 (`a2d99d73bf21b39fbb0a9a88917424ff26c2e63c`) counts full chains of orthogonal requests. The overlapping-image pair here is outside that hypothesis for m>2. Its m=2 rank-(1,1) boundary agrees numerically on the same five values.

- #4259 (`2a582d8f66d1900b22ee2cd0062ee5dca94e8f85`) proves the laminar-family full-guard law. P,Q here are neither nested nor orthogonal for m>2, so this supplies the nonnested overlapping-pair count beyond that law. The common flat q=3,m=2 boundary is 1/6 in both, checked numerically. Its open question 1 asks for the changing Schur-pair classification; this count does not classify those Schur pairs.

The preceding counting packages were produced by Nick Petalas. The retained normalizer and recursive-closure lineage is due to source527, commdata2338 and Jose Manuel; Cinna Davis supplied BIT.md; Chris R / Clear1nsight's #3950 is earlier deterministic counting context. Exact retained contract pins and credit are in the package. No unmerged source code is imported.

## Open next questions

1. A closed form or smaller invariant transfer for odd q. Start with the q=3 matrix, preserving both diagonal guard values and rank(I-A).
2. Three or more corank-one requests with orthogonal rank-one kernels. Start with a 3x3 partial Gram matrix over F2 at m=3,4.
3. A real odd-field producer and fully charged shared-header caller, including selection, emission, dispatch, dirty return and stock.

## CI notes

All local registered obligations passed. [Hosted run 39505168435](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39505168435) is green on `4728fc766b3084f3ab2f5c8543a5e74e4a12b126`: `plan` passed in 2m38s and the package `replay` passed in 1m27s. Both hosted normal/optimized scientific receipts exactly equal the local committed and Git-free export receipts, and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed` is present in the log. No check failed, and no registered local obligation was delegated to CI.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Blast radius: package. This adds one isolated research package and its bounded replay; existing scientific sources and the selected record are unchanged.
